Chachamaru"Clouds today. No good."
Kageaki"?"
Chachamaru"That sky over there. Cannot see Mount Fuji properly."
Kageaki"...Ah. This north-facing garden was designed for enjoying Fuji."
Chachamaru"Correct."
Chachamaru"From around here you get a proper view of the enormous hole in its belly・・・・・. Interesting sight."
Kageaki"I see..."
Kageaki"Now, Your Excellency."
Chachamaru"Apun?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Chachamaru"No need for such a stranger's form of address."
Kageaki"We are strangers."
Chachamaru"Cold..."
Kageaki"May I ask why you brought me all the way to Izu?"
Chachamaru"Staying in Kamakura would make trouble. Apun was on monthly defense duty for the Eastern CapitalKamakura."
Chachamaru"You could call the Hachimangu incident a failure on my part. So before Raichou and company started asking whose responsibility, I took the initiative and placed myself under voluntary confinementshut myself away at home."
Kageaki"...The Hachimangu incident..."
Chachamaru"Moriuji Ashikaga dead. One generation's great conqueror, and such an abrupt exit."
Kageaki"Is that—certain?"
Chachamaru"Kept from the publicoutside. Even inside, officially he is still missing and being searched for. But he vanished along with Hachimangu and his guards. Three days, not even a clue."
Chachamaru"Deathpassed away is settled. At Fudaraku they have started preparing a successor."
Kageaki"..."

I hoped it would not endanger him...

House arrest, for the moment?

I wanted to return to Kamakura and report everything at Hachimangu to the Prince and the Chief. If the Kubou of Horigoe refused, I would have to break out...

Rather than force, perhaps an <ruby>indirect<rt>indirect</rt></ruby> approach...

en.html:
I could not understand.
What did this general—this girl—want from me?

Enemy or ally?
Friendly, clinging like a puppy, she showed neither hostility nor an ulterior face. But she had admitted sheltering Silver Star.

Was it true?
If so, why?

What was Chachamaru Ashikaga's purpose?

...Too many mysteries.

So many that deciding where to begin was itself difficult. I could ask whatever came to mind—but how much could I trust even the answers...?

en.html: I called her name; she answered without a care. Separation. That casual manner disturbed me more than anything. How could she remain so naturalmanner? What had these two years meant to her? Even when we faced each other covered completely in armor, I had felt that gulf between our minds. Face to face in the flesh, it was still more naked. Hikaru looked at me with the same eyes as two years ago. As though nothing in our relationship had changed. Impossible—everything had changed. If she believed otherwise, that blind belief itself was madness. Hikaru was mad after all.◆ I thought so.◆ Wanted to think so・・・・. I wanted to think madness had made her the slaughtering Silver Star. Accept that, and only lamenting her misfortune and fighting her remained.
en.text:
I called her name; she answered without a care.

Separation.

That casual manner disturbed me more than anything. How could she remain so naturalmanner?

What had these two years meant to her?

Even when we faced each other covered completely in armor, I had felt that gulf between our minds. Face to face in the flesh, it was still more naked. Hikaru looked at me with the same eyes as two years ago.

As though nothing in our relationship had changed.

Impossible—everything had changed.

If she believed otherwise, that blind belief itself was madness. Hikaru was mad after all.◆
I thought so.◆
Wanted to think so・・・・.

I wanted to think madness had made her the slaughtering Silver Star. Accept that, and only lamenting her misfortune and fighting her remained.

ja.html: 名を呼べば、光は屈託のない声を返してくる。 　隔絶。 　何気ない態度こそ、何より違和感を覚えさせられて ならない。 　何故、そんなにも自然の態ていでいられるのか。 　この二年間の出来事は、光にとって何だったのか。 　互いに全身を劒冑で覆って相対していた時でさえも 感じずに済まされなかった心理の隔絶は、素肌で向き 合ってみれば尚一層赤裸々だった。 　光は二年前と同じ目で俺を見ている。 　俺との関係は何も変わっていないと、そう言うかの ように。 　そんな筈はない――何もかも変わった。 　変わらないと信じるなら、その妄信こそ狂気だ。 　光はやはり狂っている。◆ 　そう思う。◆ 　思いたい・・・・。 　狂ったからこそ殺戮の銀星号と化したのだと、そう 思いたい。 　そう思えば、後は光の悲運を嘆いて戦うだけで済む。

名を呼べば、光は屈託のない声を返してくる。

ならない。
　何故、そんなにも自然の態ていでいられるのか。

　この二年間の出来事は、光にとって何だったのか。

　互いに全身を劒冑で覆って相対していた時でさえも
感じずに済まされなかった心理の隔絶は、素肌で向き
合ってみれば尚一層赤裸々だった。

　俺との関係は何も変わっていないと、そう言うかの
ように。

　そんな筈はない――何もかも変わった。

　変わらないと信じるなら、その妄信こそ狂気だ。
　光はやはり狂っている。◆
　そう思う。◆
　思いたい・・・・。

　狂ったからこそ殺戮の銀星号と化したのだと、そう
思いたい。
　そう思えば、後は光の悲運を嘆いて戦うだけで済む。

Not madness・, not hatred・, but the reason・ of pursuing a wish, slaughtering people— Destroyingbreak the world. ...Could that be possible? And if it was—◆ ...What was I supposed to do? en.text:
But.

If... she was not mad.
If, as she said, she had done everything in her right mind・・.

Then what?

That slaughter,
that calamity,

if it had been caused not by madness—

but by hope.

If Hikaru had simply lived these two years with single-mindedsingle-minded devotion.

...Was such a thing possible?

Not madness・,
not hatred・,

but the reason・ of pursuing a wish, slaughtering people—

Destroyingbreak the world.

...Could that be possible?

And if it was—◆

...What was I supposed to do?

If my adoptive mother's death,
and the calamity scattered across Kantou,

had all arisen from Hikaru's desire for her father————

だが。

　もしも……狂っていないのなら。
　本人が言った通り、全て正気・・でしたことなら。

　どうなる？

　あの殺戮、
　あの災厄が、

　希望ゆえに引き起こされたものであったのなら。

　……それは、可能な事なのだろうか？

　狂・ではなく、
　憎・でもなく、

　願いを追い求める理・によって諸人を殺戮する――

　世界を毀こわす。

　……そんな事が可能なのか。

　もしも可能であったなら――◆

　養母の死も、
　関東に撒き散らされた災厄も、

　光の、父を求める想いゆえであったのなら――――
